title: RT-DETR-R18 vs YOLOv9-C: measured on the same protocol
dek: On the same COCO protocol, YOLOv9-C leads by 7.3 mAP points while RT-DETR-R18 runs 47.2 FPS to 42.3 on desktop GPU.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: YOLOv9-C is the more accurate detector: 57.1 vs 49.8 mAP@50-95 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, a 7.3 point lead. RT-DETR-R18 answers on speed, running 47.2 FPS to YOLOv9-C's 42.3, and it holds a memory edge at 169 vs 241 MB peak VRAM. Pick by whether accuracy or latency drives the deployment.

RT-DETR-R18 (20.18M parameters) comes from the DETR line; YOLOv9-C (25.5M) from the YOLO line. Both are permissive-licensed and evaluated at 640 px input, with verified rows on desktop GPU, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5, so this comparison spans the deploy targets that matter.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. RT-DETR-R18 and YOLOv9-C highlighted against the full field.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. YOLOv9-C measures 57.1 mAP@50-95 to RT-DETR-R18's 49.8, and the lead holds on small objects: 39.3 vs 32.7 mAP_small, a 16.75% relative gap. Where accuracy is the metric that ships, YOLOv9-C is ahead across object sizes.

On the RTX 5070 Ti, RT-DETR-R18 runs 47.2 FPS to YOLOv9-C's 42.3 in PyTorch, and the gap widens under conversion: 120.6 vs 76.7 FPS on TensorRT FP32, 113.4 vs 74.7 FPS on TensorRT FP16. On Jetson Orin the split is wider still: 10.2 vs 6.4 FPS.

The order does not swap. RT-DETR-R18 leads on throughput and YOLOv9-C on accuracy across 4 runtimes and 3 hardware platforms with verified data, from the RTX 5070 Ti down to the Raspberry Pi 5, where both fall under 1 FPS.

Pick YOLOv9-C when detection accuracy is the deliverable, including scenes full of small objects, and the extra 241 vs 169 MB VRAM fits the budget. Pick RT-DETR-R18 when throughput or memory is the constraint: it is faster on every GPU runtime measured and on Jetson Orin. Both ship under permissive licenses, so licensing does not decide it.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRr18.pt")  # 20.18M params, 49.8 mAP@50-95
yolo9 = LibreYOLO("LibreYOLO9c.pt")      # 25.5M params, 57.1 mAP@50-95

results = yolo9("image.jpg")
